newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia 96/97 sorghum output down 29 pct - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: Australia 96/97 sorghum output down 29 pct - ABARE.

text.p: Australian sorghum production is estimated at 1.1 million tonnes for 1996/97, down 29 percent from 1995/96, official forecaster the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its Australian Crop Report.
ABARE is predicting a sorghum crop of 1.37 million tonnes in 1997/98. Production in 1995/96 amounted to 1.56 million tonnes.
The lower 1996/97 production reflected a reduced area sown to sorghum because of dry conditions during most of the summer planting period, it said.

However, excellent rains in the last week of February enabled late season plantings in central Queensland and boosted subsoil moisture levels throughout Queensland and northern New South Wales (NSW), it said.
Although harvesting was yet to start in central Queensland, the delay to plantings and the hot, dry autumn had resulted in expectations of below-average yields, it said.
In southern Queensland and northern NSW, most of the crops were sown early. February rains ensured that the crops finished well, it said.
